title: Contains Duplicate
description:
# Contains Duplicate

Given an integer array `nums`, return `true` if any value appears **at least twice** in the array, and return `false` if every element is distinct.

## Example 1:

**Input:** nums = [1,2,3,1]
**Output:** true

## Example 2:

**Input:** nums = [1,2,3,4]
**Output:** false

## Example 3:

**Input:** nums = [1,1,1,3,3,4,3,2,4,2]
**Output:** true

## Constraints:

*   `1 <= nums.length <= 10^5`
*   `-10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9`

solutions.name: HashSet - One Pass
solutions.description:
## Approach

Scan the array once and keep every value that has already appeared in a `HashSet`. Before inserting the current value, ask whether it is already in the set. If it is, the duplicate condition is satisfied immediately and we can return `true`.

## Key Insight

This problem only asks whether a duplicate exists, not how many duplicates there are. A set is therefore the right state: it records membership and lets us stop as soon as the first repeated value is seen.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Sorting
solutions.description:
## Approach

Sort the array, then compare each element with its previous neighbor. Sorting moves equal values next to each other, so any duplicate will be detected by one adjacent comparison.

## Key Insight

This approach trades extra hashing state for ordering. It is useful when mutating the input is acceptable or when sorting is already part of a larger pipeline, but it is slower than the one-pass hash-set solution.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n log n)
- Space Complexity: O(1) to O(n), depending on the sorting implementation

solutions.name: Brute Force
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use two nested loops to compare every pair of different indices. If any pair contains the same value, return `true`; if all pairs are checked without a match, every value is distinct.

## Key Insight

This is the correctness baseline. It makes the definition of a duplicate explicit, which is useful for learning and for very small inputs, but it does not scale to the stated constraints.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n^2)
- Space Complexity: O(1)
